EICMA 2026 • Benelli Showed the World Its New Tornado Naked Tre 903 Concept at EICMA 2026 and It's a Triple!
Brabus 800 Shaves 0.1 Sec off the 0–60 Mph Over a Porsche Turbo S It's Built on, for Twice the Price
37 photos
Photo: Brabus
"My German ragtop sportscar isn't making enough power. Or isn't going fast enough. Or it's too slow off the line. Or something... CAN YOU DO SOMETHING ABOUT THAT? " said probably only owners who complained to Brabus about their regular Porsche 911 Turbo S, but didn’t get the BRABUS 820 from four years back. Guess what the German tuner did? Instead of calling a spiritual enlightenment coach to guide these speed-addled billionaires, the speed scientists in Bottrop grabbed their wrenches and built yet another 800-hp hair dryer.
Long before anyone decided that the 992.2 generation needed an 800-horsepower intervention, Brabus already possessed an irresistible urge to meddle with Stuttgart's crown jewel. Consider their previous exploit, the BRABUS 820 Cabriolet based on the 991.2 generation.
That machine took a standard 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six and extracted a blistering 820 hp and 950 Nm (700 lb-ft) of torque through custom turbochargers and ECU mapping, rocketing to 100 kph in 2.5 seconds and topping out at 340 kph (211 mph). It proved beyond all doubt that subtlety was merely a suggestion in the dictionary of Bottrop.
Yet time marches on, and factory engineers eventually caught up, introducing the latest 992.2 Porsche 911 Turbo S Cabriolet. Fresh out of Zuffenhausen with a base price of $284,300, this drop-top weapon packs a 3.6-liter twin-turbocharged 6-cylinder boxer engine assisted by a 400-volt T-Hybrid system.
Photo: Brabus With two electric turbochargers and an electric motor nestled inside its 8-speed dual-clutch transmission, the stock convertible produces 711 PS, or 701 hp, and 800 Nm. In imperial human terms, 800 Nm equals 590 lb-ft of instantaneous torque, fed by a compact 1.9 kWh battery and routed through all-wheel drive.
The standard Cabriolet rockets from 0 to 100 kph in 2.6 seconds, while the $270,300 Coupé takes 2.5 seconds and hits 200 kph in 8.4 seconds. Both reach 322 kph, or 200 mph, which is apparently pedestrian when you are late for a Monaco yacht party.
Naturally, Brabus looked at the most powerful production 911 in history and decided Porsche engineers were being exceptionally too humble about the capacity of their flat-six masterpiece. Enter the Brabus 800, a comprehensive conversion offered for both the Cabriolet and Coupé.
Photo: Brabus If you happen to be browsing their inventory, you will discover that this automotive fever dream commands a staggering price tag of €482,713.63 before local taxes. That’s about $540,757 in Legal Money of the United States. It is also about 200k Euros (225k USD) more than a factory Porsche. The good news is the coupe is only €419,580 ($470,000).
By installing the PowerXtra P36-800 performance upgrade onto the 3,591-cc flat-six engine, the tuner extracted an extra 65 kW, or 89 hp, pushing total hybrid system output to a glorious 588 kW, or 800 hp.
Peak torque simultaneously climbs by 100 Nm to a tectonic 900 Nm, or 664 lb-ft, ensuring the driver’s toupee reaches destination before the wearer does. That newfound muscle shaves 0.1 seconds off the factory sprint, launching the Brabus 800 Cabriolet from 0 to 100 kph in 2.5 seconds and the Coupé in 2.4 seconds. Top speed remains electronically capped at 322 kph, or 200 mph, with consumption at 11.5 l/100 km (20 mpg).
Photo: Brabus Because saving 0.1 seconds is meaningless if the neighbors cannot hear your financial superiority from two blocks away, Brabus swaps the standard titanium muffler for a valve-controlled sports exhaust system. Its quadruple rounded tailpipes sit seamlessly inside the rear diffuser, letting drivers toggle between a polite whisper and a volcanic boxer roar at the push of a button.
Emitting 261 g/km of CO2 never sounded so theatrical or mechanically intoxicating with the roof down. Speaking of carbon: visual subtlety was never on the menu either, yet the newly developed exposed-carbon aerodynamic package is genuinely brilliant engineering. Available in glossy or matte finishes, every component works in harmony with the factory active aerodynamics rather than just looking cool.
Up front, a carbon-fiber spoiler with raised side flaps reduces axle lift at high speeds, accompanied by bespoke carbon fascia inserts, vertical air intake louvers, and a complete carbon-fiber front hood. Along the flanks, carbon-fiber mirror housings and sculpted side skirt attachments visually stretch the widebody silhouette, making the car look like it is breaking speed limits while parked outside a café.
Photo: Brabus Out back, an elevated carbon-fiber rear spoiler teams up with the active wing system to pile on extra downforce, while a carbon-fiber rear diffuser and a carbon rear cover bearing raised Brabus lettering between the taillights finish the transformation . This rolling sculpture also marks the world premiere of the center-lock forged Brabus Monoblock ZL Platinum Edition wheels, featuring five pairs of delicate Y-shaped spokes finished in glossy black with polished surfaces.
Measuring 9.5J x 21 inches up front and 12J x 22 inches in back, they wear Continental SportContact 7 tires sized 255/30 ZR 21 and 335/25 ZR 22, tucked under height-adjustable sport springs lowering it by 25 millimeters (near as makes no difference one inch). Crucially, those adjustable springs are calibrated to work seamlessly with the factory active dampers, sharpening turn-in without turning your spine into a torsion bar over cobblestones.
Inside the cabin, the Brabus Masterpiece saddlery replaces almost every inch of standard trim with hand-stitched black leather accented by contrasting gray piping and a gray 12-o'clock steering wheel marker. The seats, floor mats, and trunk mat showcase intricate Dynamic Diamond Double quilting and perforations. Even the upper and lower dashboard, steering wheel airbag cover, center console, A-pillars, sun visors, and seat back panels are swathed in supple hide.
Photo: Brabus To remind passengers who built this cockpit, Brabus Signature Carbon adorns the dashboard, console, steering wheel, and doors. Aluminum pedal pads, an anodized footrest glowing with red Brabus lettering, and carbon-fiber sill plates with logos alternating between red and white complete this opulent bespoke interior makeover.
Did anyone on Earth genuinely need an 800 hp hybrid Porsche 911 Turbo S Cabriolet costing nearly 400,000 Euros? If they did, where exactly would they do 200 flat-out mph with the breeze hurricaning their hairline behind their ears? Then again, there’s a Chinese EV that just broke the 500-kph barrier (310 mph).
That is precisely why the Brabus 800 is such a triumph. Rather than ruining an icon with garish gimmicks, Bottrop elevated every dynamic, aerodynamic, and tactile metric with obsessive German precision. It is an outrageously fast, impeccably tailored masterpiece that turns a clinical Stuttgart supercar into an unapologetically wicked work of automotive art.
Which doesn't always mean going above, ahead, beyond what's behind. Brabus actually took a small step back, downgrading from the previous Porsche 911 Turbo S build to this 20-hp, 11 mph tamer, 800-hp rocket.
Via // Brabus
